title: smart-routing-fallback-debug-scratchpad-jordan-reyes
content:
Context:
- Small production incident on 2025-09-17 23:12 UTC where smart routing triggered a regional failover for eu-west-1 -> us-east-1 for a handful of requests.
- Impact: ~0.2% of requests saw 2-5x latency increase and ~120 errors (503 / model-variant errors) over a 14-minute window.
- Alerting: SLO page spike + automatic fallback kicked in but traffic was routed to a model variant that returned tokenization errors for a subset of customers.

What I saw (quick timeline):
- 23:11: healthcheck notices small drop in capacity for eu-west-1 pool (GC / eviction events in node logs).
- 23:12: smart-routing controller evaluated policy: prefer-low-latency -> eu-west-1 degraded -> failover to us-east-1.
- 23:12:20: some requests start erroring with tokenizer/mismatch errors (see snippets).
- 23:26: fallback policy rolled back to degraded region, traffic normalized.

Commands I ran / outputs (most useful ones):
- curl to health endpoints
  $ curl -sS https://infra-eu-west-1.health.redwood.local/health | jq .
  {
    "gpu_pools": {"available": 6, "pending_evictions": 2},
    "runtime_ok": true
  }

- kubectl logs (serving-router) around 23:12
  $ kubectl -n routing logs deploy/smart-router-2 -c controller --since=30m | grep -i "failover" -n
  134: 2025-09-17T23:12:17Z controller: initiating failover region=eu-west-1 target=us-east-1 reason=pool_capacity_drop
  137: 2025-09-17T23:12:20Z router: routed request request_id=rr-0x7a token_count=240 target_variant=redwood-v2-q8 mismatch=true

- sample error snippet from serving logs (tokenizer mismatch):
  ERROR [2025-09-17T23:12:20.456Z] serve: request=rr-0x7a variant=redwood-v2-q8 err="tokenizer: vocab mismatch: expected 50265 tokens, got 50002"

- query to routing meta store (Redis) to check variant metadata TTLs
  $ redis-cli -h routing-meta-1 GET variant:redwood-v2-q8:tokenizer_hash
  "abc123-def456"  
  (note: eu-west-1 had stale variant metadata for redwood-v2-q8 with older tokenizer hash)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Stale variant metadata in the routing metadata store (Redis/Consul) caused controller to consider the us-east-1 variant compatible, but runtime on us-east-1 had a different tokenizer build -> tokenization errors.
   - Evidence: tokenizer_hash mismatch in logs and redis GET returned an older hash for the variant used in failover.
2) Race between model rollout and region tagging: a new quantized build (q8) was pushed to us-east-1 but automation did not update the variant compatibility tags consistently across regions.
   - Evidence: recent CI deploy (see GH commit) touches build steps + tagging script.
3) Capacity estimation bug: short-lived pod evictions in eu-west-1 triggered failover even though local prefix-cache could have healed latency.
   - Evidence: GC/eviction logs show 2 pending evictions but average latency per node remained below SLO for 95% of requests.
4) Time skew / clock drift causing TTLs to appear expired in controller evaluation window.

Repro steps (dev environment):
- Setup two-region dev cluster with variant metadata mismatch:
  1) deploy variant redwood-test-v1 with tokenizer_hash=H1 in region A, H2 in region B
  2) force controller to prefer A then simulate capacity drop in A (kill a replica)
  3) confirm failover routes to B and observe tokenizer mismatch errors

Quick experiments tried (results):
- Forcing metadata refresh on routing nodes in us-east-1 fixed immediate errors:
  $ redis-cli -h routing-meta-1 SET variant:redwood-v2-q8:tokenizer_hash "abc123-def456" (match)
  -> errors stopped within ~10s for new requests.
- Rolling restart of controller nodes prevented new failovers for ~30 minutes but not root cause.
- Replaying traffic with header X-Region-Prefer:eu-west-1 returned expected latency profile (sanity check).

Immediate mitigations (done):
- Added a temporary pre-failover check: require tokenizer_hash equality across candidate variants before sending traffic. (hotfix deployed to controller at 2025-09-18 02:30 UTC)
- Backfilled missing metadata in routing meta store for redwood-v2-q8 across regions.
- Opened urgency ticket JIRA-INFRA-789 and notified release-eng + applied ops.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Patch: add strong consistency write/verify step in release pipeline to ensure variant metadata (tokenizer_hash, vocab_size, tokenizer_version) are atomically updated across regions (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/342).
- Long-term: change fallback policy to prefer model-compatibility checks (tokenizer+vocab) before region selection; currently policy is capacity/latency-first.
- Investigate capacity estimator heuristics; ensure short GC/eviction blips don't trigger full-region failover unless sustained > X minutes.
- Add integration test in canary pipeline: cross-region metadata mismatch scenario should fail the rollout.
- Postmortem draft: assign to Maya and Ethan; target publish by 2025-09-22.

Notes to self / followups: 
- Check time skew on controller nodes (chrony/ntpd): ran ntpq -p on eu-west nodes, need to check us-east nodes too.
- Verify Redis replication lag during incident window (could explain stale read).
- Confirm whether fallback policy logs include variant metadata snapshot at decision time; if not, add it for future breadcrumbs.

Pieces of interest / links: 
- GH commit that probably introduced tagging race: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/commit/3a7b2f1
- JIRA: JIRA-INFRA-789 (incident owner: Jordan)
- Confluence runbook: CONFLUENCE:smart-routing-runbook

Open questions (for postmortem):
- Should we change priority: compatibility checks vs latency SLAs? Is 99.9th latency more important than correctness for fallback?
- What is acceptable window for metadata consistency across regions for fast rollouts?

Scratch / quick commands for followups:
- redis-cli -h routing-meta-1 HGETALL variant:redwood-v2-q8
- kubectl -n routing exec -it smart-router-2 -- curl -sS localhost:8080/decision?req=rr-0x7a
- aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn <tg> --query 'TargetHealthDescriptions[*].{Id:Target.Id,State:TargetHealth.State}'

End of notes.

(rough, keep iterative. will clean for postmortem draft.)
